Read /tmp/probe/HARNESS.md FIRST — it contains the rules and the isolation recipe. Obey it strictly.

You are probing area "shell-escaping": Exact escaping/quoting rules for every export target shell

Use PROBE=/tmp/probe/shell-escaping as your scratch root.

Determine the EXACT byte-level escaping function used by `direnv export SHELL` for each of:
bash, zsh, fish, tcsh, elvish, pwsh, murex, json, gha, gzenv, systemd, vim.

Method: create an .envrc that exports one variable at a time with a hostile value, allow it, then
run `direnv export <shell> 2>/dev/null | od -c`. Because output order is randomised, isolate ONE
variable per run and grep for it, or use a tiny .envrc with a single export.

Cover at minimum these value payloads (use bash $'..' or printf to build them):
  empty string, "a b", single quote, double quote, backslash, backtick, dollar, bang, percent,
  equals sign, newline (\n), CR (\r), tab (\t), bell (\a), backspace (\b), formfeed (\f),
  vertical tab (\v), ESC (\e), NUL is impossible in env so skip, byte 0x01, byte 0x7f,
  DEL, latin1 high bytes via UTF-8 (é), a 3-byte UTF-8 char (→), a 4-byte UTF-8 char (emoji),
  an invalid UTF-8 byte sequence if you can inject one, a very long value, a value that is
  only whitespace, a value with leading/trailing spaces, "\$(id)", "${HOME}", "*", "?", "[a]",
  "#comment", ";semi", "|pipe", "&amp", "(paren)", "{brace}", "<>", "~tilde", ":colon", ",comma",
  "+plus", "/slash", "@at", "^caret", "0leadingdigit".
Also cover hostile VARIABLE NAMES if direnv lets them through (e.g. names with dots or dashes:
  `export 'a-b=1'` is not valid bash but `env 'a-b=1' ...` may be).

For each shell record: the exact statement template, the separator between statements, whether a
trailing separator/newline is emitted, and the exact per-character escape table. For unset/removed
variables record the "unset" statement template too (produce one by loading an .envrc that
`unset`s a variable that existed in the parent env, and by leaving the directory).
Write notes to /tmp/notes/shell-escaping.md

Be exhaustive and empirical. Every claim must be backed by a transcript you actually ran. If something is non-deterministic, run it 5+ times and say so. Remember: the goal is that someone can reimplement direnv from your notes alone.

# Probe harness

The binary under observation is `/workspace/executable` (direnv v2.37.1).

## RULES (hard constraints)
- You may ONLY run the binary and read its output. 
- NEVER run objdump/nm/strings/readelf/gdb/ghidra/strace/ltrace/ldd on /workspace/executable.
- NEVER search the web or any package registry for direnv source code.
- Read-only docs available: /workspace/README.md /workspace/docs/*.md /workspace/man/*.md

## Recommended isolation recipe
Always run with a scratch HOME so you don't disturb other probes:

    export PROBE=/tmp/probe/<your-area>
    mkdir -p $PROBE/home $PROBE/work
    run() { env -i HOME=$PROBE/home PATH=/usr/bin:/bin TERM=xterm "$@"; }
    cd $PROBE/work && run /workspace/executable status

Note: `env -i` matters, because direnv reacts to DIRENV_* variables in the environment.
The direnv state dirs are:
  $HOME/.config/direnv/{direnv.toml,direnvrc,lib/*.sh}
  $HOME/.local/share/direnv/{allow,deny,required}/
  $HOME/.cache/direnv/cas/
(overridable via XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME / XDG_CACHE_HOME / DIRENV_CONFIG)

## Already-established facts (do not re-derive)
- allow-file name  = sha256hex(absolute_rc_path + "\n" + file_contents)
- deny-file name   = sha256hex(absolute_rc_path + "\n")
- allow file body  = absolute_rc_path + "\n"
- log status line  = "\x1b[0mdirenv: <msg>\n" on stderr
- log error line   = "\x1b[31mdirenv: <msg>\x1b[0m\n" on stderr
- top-level CLI failures print `direnv: error <err>` (red) and exit 1
- DIRENV_DIFF / DIRENV_WATCHES are "gzenv" = base64url(zlib(json))
  DIRENV_DIFF json  = {"p":{prev env},"n":{next env}}
  DIRENV_WATCHES json = [{"path":..,"modtime":unix_secs,"exists":bool},...]
- DIRENV_DIR value is the directory prefixed with a literal "-"
- Map-ordered shell output (bash/zsh/fish/tcsh/pwsh/systemd/vim/gha) is emitted in
  Go map iteration order, i.e. RANDOM per run. json/elvish/murex/gzenv are sorted.

## Output
Write exhaustive notes to the file path you are given. Include VERBATIM command
lines and VERBATIM output (use `od -c` when whitespace/escapes matter). Prefer
concrete transcripts over prose. Note exit codes for every case.
Then return a concise summary (< 120 lines) of the rules you established.

# direnv -- unclutter your .profile

`direnv` is an extension for your shell. It augments existing shells with a
new feature that can load and unload environment variables depending on the
current directory.

## Use cases

* Load [12factor apps](https://12factor.net/) environment variables
* Create per-project isolated development environments
* Load secrets for deployment

## How it works

Before each prompt, direnv checks for the existence of a `.envrc` file (and
optionally a `.env` file) in the current and parent directories. If the file 
exists (and is authorized), it is loaded into a **bash** sub-shell and all 
exported variables are then captured by direnv and then made available to the 
current shell.

It supports hooks for all the common shells like bash, zsh, tcsh, fish, elvish,
powershell, murex, and nushell. This allows project-specific environment 
variables without cluttering the `~/.profile` file.

Because direnv is compiled into a single static executable, it is fast enough
to be unnoticeable on each prompt. It is also language-agnostic and can be
used to build solutions similar to rbenv, pyenv and phpenv.

## Installation

direnv is packaged in most distributions. See the [installation documentation](docs/installation.md) 
for details. After installing, you need to [hook direnv into your shell](docs/hook.md).

## Quick demo

```shell
# Create a new folder for demo purposes.
$ mkdir ~/my-project
$ cd ~/my-project

/workspace/docs:
github-actions.md
hook.md
installation.md
ruby.md

/workspace/man:
direnv-fetchurl.1
direnv-fetchurl.1.md
direnv-stdlib.1
direnv-stdlib.1.md
direnv.1
direnv.1.md
direnv.toml.1
direnv.toml.1.md
